page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Chemical Equilibrium, Acids and Bases · 2 marks

steps.label: The definition
lines: In a reversible reaction, equilibrium is the
state at which the rate of the forward
reaction equals the rate of the backward
reaction. The concentrations of all the
steps.why: Equal rates is the cause and constant concentrations is the result — the definition must contain the equality of the two rates, not only the constancy.
common_mistakes: Writing that the reaction stops at equilibrium. Both reactions continue.
Writing that the concentrations of reactants and products become equal. They become constant, not equal to each other.
steps.memory_tip: Rates equal, amounts steady. Two runs at the same speed in opposite directions look like standing still.
steps.margin_note: The words equal rates must appear in the definition.

steps.label: Why it is called dynamic

lines.text: Both reactions continue at equal rates, so the equilibrium is called dynamic

lines: NH₃ is formed and decomposed at the same
rate, so its amount does not change.
steps.why: Dynamic means in motion. Molecular change continues in both directions even though nothing appears to change from outside — that is the exact point this question tests.
common_mistakes: Calling the equilibrium static because nothing appears to change from outside.
steps.memory_tip: Dynamic means moving. The reaction keeps running in both directions; only the totals stand still.
steps.margin_note: One example written with the ⇌ arrow supports the definition.

insider_note: A three-star definition where the mark is lost by writing that the reaction stops — the examiner looks for both reactions continuing at equal rates.
